name: Text Encode
description: Turns a prompt into conditioning for the Sampler, with the model's text encoder, and carries the reference pictures of an edit, or the first frame of a clip, to it. Kept while only the sampling changes, so a new seed does not encode the prompt again.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.label: Negative prompt
inputs.description: What the image should not show. Used only when the Sampler's guidance is not 1.

inputs.name: references
inputs.label: References
inputs.description: Pictures to edit or take from, for a model that edits (FLUX.2 Klein, Qwen-Image Edit, Krea 2 with an edit LoRA). Each goes to the model at most a megapixel, unless Reference size is exact; Resize to Megapixels sets it.

inputs.name: reference_size
inputs.label: Reference size
inputs.description: Auto: the engine scales each reference to at most a megapixel (and the output's area), to a multiple of 16, before the model sees it. Exact: each keeps the size the graph gave it, as ComfyUI's edit does; a side that is not a multiple of 16 (32 for Qwen-Image) is cut from the middle down to one, as ComfyUI's VAE Encode does. Krea 2 Edit ignores it: each reference is fitted to the output.

inputs.name: edit_format
inputs.label: Edit format
inputs.description: How an edit model takes the references; models it is not for ignore it. Default: the engine's own layout (the references also go to the text encoder when it has a vision tower; for Krea 2, the layout of ostris's LoRAs). Moss-Image-Edit, for MOSS-Image: ComfyUI's format of that name, which the edit LoRA is trained for: the references go to the model through the VAE only, with no vision tokens, anchored at the text start. Up to four references. Krea 2 Edit, for Krea 2 with the Identity Edit or General Edit LoRA (ComfyUI-Krea2Edit): each reference is fitted to the output and goes to the model at the current step, the text encoder sees it at Vision size, and Reference boost and placement apply. With two references the first is the scene, the second the person.

inputs.name: ref_boost
inputs.label: Reference boost
inputs.description: Krea 2 Edit: how hard the output copies the last reference (the person, or the only picture). 1 is as trained, higher keeps more of its look, lower loosens it. The LoRA's author suggests 4 for General Edit and 2 for Identity Edit; above about 10 removals and replacements start to fail.

inputs.name: ref_position
inputs.label: Reference placement
inputs.description: Krea 2 Edit: where the last reference sits for the model. Aligned pins it on the output's layout, as the LoRAs were trained: for edits that keep the picture. Beside puts it next to the output: the person keeps their look but can be restaged freely. Bag of features is experimental: its content without its layout.

inputs.name: scene_boost
inputs.label: Scene boost
inputs.description: Krea 2 Edit with two references: Reference boost for the first (the scene). No effect with one.

inputs.name: scene_position
inputs.label: Scene placement
inputs.description: Krea 2 Edit with two references: Reference placement for the first (the scene). To put a person in a scene: scene aligned, person beside.

inputs.name: vision_size
inputs.label: Vision size
inputs.description: Krea 2 Edit: the long side, in pixels, of each reference the text encoder sees (a larger one is scaled down; 0 keeps it). Lower follows the instruction more, higher keeps more likeness: try 1024 for people, 512 for a stubborn scene change. Trained at 384 to 768.

inputs.name: first_frame
inputs.label: First frame
inputs.description: The picture a clip starts from, for an image-to-video model (Wan 2.2 I2V or TI2V). It is scaled to cover the size of Clip and cut from the middle.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.label: Clip
inputs.description: The Empty Video Latent the clip is made from: with a first frame, the size, length and rate the picture is encoded for. Wire the same one to the Sampler.
